skill.name: verification-before-completion
skill.description: Requires fresh verification evidence before claiming work is complete, fixed, passing, or ready for review.
skill.summary: Prompts agents to verify commands and evidence before making completion claims.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences or verification-related prose. No evidence found of executable commands, reconnaissance behavior, prompt injection, data exfiltration, or malicious intent.

remediation.issue: Static scanners may misread Markdown fences as executable backtick usage.
remediation.suggestion: Label fenced examples as text, or avoid bare fences around policy statements when marketplace scanning is required.

remediation.issue: Forceful wording may be harder for reviewers to distinguish from operational commands.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the verification rule, but use neutral wording where possible to improve marketplace review clarity.

content.value_statement: Agents can claim success before checking real evidence. This skill requires fresh verification commands and evidence before completion claims.
actual_capabilities: Requires fresh command output before claiming tests, builds, or fixes are complete.
Maps common claims to the evidence needed to support them.
Flags weak phrases such as should, probably, and seems to.
Guides agents to read full output and check exit status before reporting.
Supports verification before commits, pull requests, and task handoffs.
limitations: It does not run commands by itself.
It cannot prove correctness without project-specific verification commands.
It depends on the agent reading and reporting output accurately.
It may add time to small changes that still need verification.

use_cases.title: Pre-Commit Verification
use_cases.description: Confirm tests, lint checks, and build output before committing code or opening a pull request.

use_cases.title: Agent Handoff Review
use_cases.description: Check another agent report against file changes and verification evidence before accepting completion.

use_cases.title: Bug Fix Confirmation
use_cases.description: Verify the original failure mode and related regression tests before saying a bug is fixed.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Verification Check
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner use after a small task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Before you claim this task is complete, identify the command that proves it. Run it, read the full output, and report the result.

prompt_templates.title: Fix Evidence Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate use after a bug fix.
prompt_templates.prompt: Verify the original bug is fixed. Run the relevant test or reproduction, include the observed result, and state any remaining risk.

prompt_templates.title: Pre-PR Quality Gate
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced use before opening a pull request.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the full verification set for this change. Check tests, build, and changed requirements before stating whether the PR is ready.

prompt_templates.title: Delegated Agent Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced use when another agent reported success.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the agent report against the diff and fresh verification output. Accept only claims supported by evidence from this session.

output_examples.input: The agent finished a bug fix and wants to say all tests pass.
output_examples.output: The response names the test command, reports fresh output, and only claims success when the output supports it.

output_examples.input: A build looks likely to pass because linting passed.
output_examples.output: The response rejects the assumption, runs the build command, and reports the actual build result.

output_examples.input: Another agent says it completed a delegated task.
output_examples.output: The response checks the changed files, verifies expected behavior, and reports confirmed work plus unresolved gaps.

best_practices: Run the exact command that proves the claim you plan to make.
Read the full output and check failures before summarizing status.
Report uncertainty plainly when verification is incomplete or blocked.
anti_patterns: Do not claim success from confidence, memory, or partial checks.
Do not treat a linter result as proof that a build passes.
Do not accept another agent report without independent verification.

faq.question: Does this skill run tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It tells the agent to choose and run the right verification command before making completion claims.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it before reporting completion, creating a pull request, committing code, or accepting delegated work.

faq.question: Does it replace project test instructions?
faq.answer: No. It helps enforce verification, but the project still defines the correct commands and acceptance criteria.

faq.question: Can it help with non-code tasks?
faq.answer: Yes. It can require evidence for any completion claim, but it is strongest for coding workflows.

faq.question: Why does it mention agent reports?
faq.answer: It warns that reports from other agents still need review against real changes and fresh evidence.

faq.question: Is this skill safe for marketplace use?
faq.answer: The reviewed file contains workflow guidance only. The flagged command and reconnaissance patterns were false positives.
